facts.statement: The genus Ctenochasma was first described by Christian Erich Hermann von Meyer in 1851.
facts.quote: authority: Meyer, 1851

facts.statement: Ctenochasma lived during the Late Jurassic period.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Late Jurassic

facts.statement: Ctenochasma is a genus of pterosaur belonging to the suborder Pterodactyloidea.
facts.quote: Ctenochasma (meaning "comb jaw") is a genus of Late Jurassic ctenochasmatid pterosaur belonging to the suborder Pterodactyloidea.

facts.statement: Fossils of Ctenochasma have been found in the Solnhofen Limestone of Bavaria, the Purbeck Group of northeastern Germany, and the Calcaires tâchetés of eastern France.
facts.quote: Their fossilized remains have been found in the Solnhofen Limestone of Bavaria, Germany, the "Purbeck Group" of northeastern Germany, and the Calcaires tâchetés of eastern France.

facts.statement: Adult Ctenochasma had over 400 long, thin, curved, and closely packed teeth lining an elongated snout.
facts.quote: Ctenochasma is distinguished mainly by its numerous (over 400 in adults) long, thin, curved and closely packed teeth, which lined its elongated and narrow snout.

facts.statement: The closely packed teeth formed a comb-like basket traditionally thought to be used for filter feeding, though it lacked the pumping mechanism found in related species.
facts.quote: The teeth were so closely packed that they formed a comb, and in adults they projected outward away from the jaws, forming a basket; traditionally, these are thought to indicate a filter feeding lifestyle, straining water through the teeth in order to capture and eat small invertebrates, but unlike the related Pterodaustro it lacks adaptations that would form a pumping mechanism.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest the tooth profile indicates a spoonbill-like lifestyle for catching small prey.
facts.quote: Instead, the spatulate profile formed by the teeth probably indicate a spoonbill-like lifestyle, increasing the surface area of the jaws in order to catch small prey.

facts.statement: The smallest species, C. elegans, reached a maximum adult wingspan of 1.9 meters.
facts.quote: The smallest species, Ctenochasma elegans, had a maximum wingspan of 1.9 m as an adult.

facts.statement: Adult Ctenochasma possessed a bony crest along the skull that was absent in juveniles.
facts.quote: Adult Ctenochasma had a bony crest along the skull, though this is not found in juveniles.

facts.statement: Comparisons of scleral rings suggest Ctenochasma may have been nocturnal with activity patterns similar to modern nocturnal seabirds.
facts.quote: Comparisons between the scleral rings of both Ctenochasma elegans and Ctenochasma taqueti and modern birds and reptiles suggest that these taxa may have been nocturnal, and may have had activity patterns similar to modern nocturnal seabirds.

facts.statement: Ctenochasma had larger wings than other ctenochasmatoids and may have flown like modern skuas.
facts.quote: Compared to other ctenochasmatoids, it had larger wings, and may have displayed a flying style comparable to that of modern skuas.

facts.statement: Ctenochasma is classified within the family Ctenochasmatidae, subfamily Ctenochasmatinae, as the sister taxon to the tribe Pterodaustrini.
facts.quote: In the analysis, they recovered Ctenochasma within the family Ctenochasmatidae, more precisely within the subfamily Ctenochasmatinae, sister taxon to the tribe Pterodaustrini.

facts.statement: Ctenochasma is distinguished by numerous long, thin teeth (about 400 in adults) aligned in an elongated, narrow snout.
facts.quote: Ctenochasma se distingue principalmente por sus largos y delgados numerosos dientes (cerca de 400 en los adultos), agrupados muy cerca unos de otros, los cuales se alineaban en un hocico alargado y estrecho.

facts.statement: The smallest species, C. elegans, had a wingspan of only 25 cm.
facts.quote: La especie más pequeña, Ctenochasma elegans, tenía una envergadura de solo 25 cm.

facts.statement: Ctenochasma is distinguished by a mouth containing up to 260 teeth.
facts.quote: Ctenochasma se distingue por su boca con hasta 260 dientes.

facts.statement: Fossils of Ctenochasma have been found in the Solnhofen Limestone of Bavaria, Germany, and eastern France.
facts.quote: Sus restos fosilizados han sido hallados en la Caliza de Solnhofen de Baviera (Alemania) y el oriente de Francia.

facts.statement: The genus Ctenochasma was named by the German paleontologist Christian Erich Hermann von Meyer in 1852.
facts.quote: El nombre Ctenochasma fue acuñado por el paleontólogo alemán Christian Erich Hermann von Meyer en 1852

facts.statement: The genus was originally based on a single lower jaw filled with crowded teeth.
facts.quote: basándose en una única mandíbula inferior llena de dientes apiñados

facts.statement: The species C. gracile was named by Oppel in 1862 based on a fragmentary skull.
facts.quote: Una segunda especie, C. gracile, fue nombrada por Oppel en 1862 basándose en un cráneo fragmentario

facts.statement: The species now known as C. elegans was originally described and named Pterodactylus elegans by Wagner.
facts.quote: Pterodactylus elegans por Wagner

facts.statement: The species is currently known as Ctenochasma elegans because it was named before C. gracile.
facts.quote: Debido a que la especie elegans fue nombrada antes que gracile, la especie es conocida como Ctenochasma elegans

facts.statement: The species C. porocristata was named by Paul de Buisonjé in 1981.
facts.quote: Una especie adicional, C. porocristata, fue nombrada por Paul de Buisonjé en 1981

facts.statement: The species C. porocristata is distinguished mainly by a crest along its snout, which is linked to growth or sex rather than being a species-specific trait.
facts.quote: esta se diferencia mayormente por la presencia de una cresta a lo largo de su hocico, la cual se ha demostrado que es un rasgo vinculado al crecimiento o al sexo, más que a la especie

facts.statement: A fourth species of Ctenochasma was initially described but not named by Philippe Taquet in 1972.
facts.quote: Una cuarta especie de Ctenochasma fue inicialmente descrita (pero no nombrada) por Philippe Taquet en 1972

facts.statement: A unique specimen consisting of a partial skull with a complete neurocranium was found in France.
facts.quote: Un espécimen único, consistente en un cráneo parcial con el neurocráneo completo, fue hallado en Francia

facts.statement: The species was formally named C. taqueti by Christopher Bennett in 2007.
facts.quote: Christopher Bennett nombró a la especie C. taqueti en 2007

facts.statement: Ctenochasma belongs to the parent group Lophocratia.
facts.quote: Parent group: Lophocratia

facts.statement: Ctenochasma is classified in the class Reptilia.
facts.quote: Class: Reptilia

facts.statement: Ctenochasma lived from the Tithonian to the Berriasian, between 149.2 and 137.05 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Tithonian to Berriasian (149.2 to 137.05 million years ago)

facts.statement: There are 7 recorded fossil occurrences of Ctenochasma.
facts.quote: Fossil occurrences recorded: 7

rejected.statement: The species Ctenochasma roemeri was named by Christian Erich Hermann von Meyer in 1851 based on a single lower jaw.
rejected.quote: The name Ctenochasma was coined by the German paleontologist Christian Erich Hermann von Meyer in 1851, based on a single lower jaw full of closely packed teeth which he gave the species name Ctenochasma roemeri.
rejected.reason: statement copies the source wording: 'in 1851 based on a single lower jaw'

rejected.statement: Philippe Taquet first described a fourth species of Ctenochasma in 1972, which was later named C. taqueti in 2007.
rejected.quote: A fourth species of Ctenochasma was first described (but not named) by Philippe Taquet in 1972.
